o_L1_001: no room on either side; threshold gets the style floor material

cam_r_L1_banyo_1: no free camera point in the room; camera at the room's inner point; moved to the nearest point with 0.3 m of headroom under the sloped ceiling (1.55 m high there); blocked unavoidable
cam_r_L1_banyo_1: the lens is 0.108 m from the furniture f_L1_021 (nearer than 0.12 m, the blocked distance of the camera search): the view may be blocked (lens clearance, warning only)

guards.rule: A tall wet-room fixture (shower, tub) under a sloped ceiling must be capped or swapped to a model whose height fits the slope at its position; nothing inside may cross the roof (UL128).

When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g. SALON + AÇIK MUTFAK), the reading must split the outline into the separate rooms each label names, instead of keeping one merged room and dropping the other labels.
Every room label the documents name on a level must map to a distinct room in the model; a label whose area and anchor do not match any built room is a lost room, not a duplicate.
A balcony/terrace must carry its lounge group (seating + side table); a terrace whose main furniture group is missing is an empty, undefined space.
An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height; an all-black frame is a failed render, not a view.
A sectional sofa's parts must be joined (within 1 cm); parts standing apart are a build defect, fixed by re-joining, not by swapping the model.
An armchair's back and arms must rest against its seat (within 5 mm); a gap is a build defect, fixed by re-planning the rests, not by swapping the model.

A soft-seat model whose back or arm is not flush with its seat (gap over 5 mm) must be rebuilt by the rest plan or swapped for a model that is flush; a 5 cm gap between the rest and the seat is a build defect, not a placement one.
Scene geometry checks (S1) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S2) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S4) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S6) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

When an armchair is placed behind the back of a sofa and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that lowers plausibility is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.

When a tv_unit is placed behind the back of a piece and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that pushes it through the room outline is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.
A wardrobe that reaches through the room outline, even by a small depth, must be re-placed or resized so it stays within the room; the fit stage must keep all pieces inside the room outline.

When a table_coffee overlaps an armchair, the fit stage must re-place one of them so they do not overlap; if move_piece is refused because the overlap persists or max_tries is reached, the agent must try a different position or swap a model.
An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; the fit stage must ensure every piece's front use zone is reachable.

A sofa_corner whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; if swap_model is refused because the asset is unusable, the agent must try a different model or re-place the piece.

A seating group whose members cannot all face each other and keep a 0.60 m walkway from the door is re-solved as one unit (relayout) rather than rotated piece by piece, which only trades one orientation error for another.
A piece that crosses a room outline by 0.02 m or less is within tolerance and is not a finding.
When a coffee table overlaps a chair and every single-piece move is refused (max_tries), the seating group is re-solved as a unit so the table and chairs are placed together with clearances.

A piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the room's seating group, not by moving the single piece, which would break the group it belongs to.
A corner sofa whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the seating group; swapping to a smaller model is refused when the asset is unusable.
A stove whose back is not on a wall is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run as a unit so the counter, stove and sink are placed together against the wall with the required aisle.
A kitchen counter whose front aisle is under 0.90 m is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run so the counter is placed against the wall with a full aisle.
A sofa whose drawn footprint is 0.90 m wide by 2.13 m deep is a misread orientation: the piece is re-typed or re-placed so its long side is the seat depth, not the width.
A sofa whose back is 0.59 m off a wall and cannot be moved to a free wall span within the drawn-lock limit is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the sofa is placed against a wall.
An armchair that does not face its group is fixed by re-solving the seating group so all members face each other.
An armchair whose front zone is blocked by another armchair is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the two armchairs are placed with clear front zones.
A dining chair with under 0.81 m behind it is fixed by re-solving the dining group so the chairs have the required clearance to the wall or piece behind.
A seating group whose members are drawn overlapping or with blocked front zones must be re-solved as a unit, not rotated piece by piece.
A dining chair with less than 0.81 m behind it must be re-solved with its table, not nudged alone.
A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side in a room under 17 m2 must take a narrower model, not be shifted.
A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side must take a narrower model when the room cannot give the clearance.
A wardrobe with less than 0.80 m in front must take a shallower model when the room cannot give the opening clearance.
A shower whose drawn size is outside the product range must take a real product model that fits the bay.
A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side must take a model that fits the room's side clearance.
An armchair that stands behind the back of its group must be re-solved with the group, not rotated alone.
A sofa whose front zone is blocked by another piece must be re-solved with the group.
A coffee table not in front of the sofa must be re-solved with the seating group.
A dining chair with less than 0.81 m behind it must be re-solved with its table.
A tv_unit 1 m off a wall must be re-solved with the room's media group.

A seating group is solved as one unit: the armchairs are placed facing the group centre (sofa/TV axis), never with their back to a group member; a rotation that only swaps one F4 for another (wall or group) is refused and the whole group is re-solved.

A seating group is solved as one unit: the armchairs are placed facing the group centre (sofa/TV axis), never with their back to a group member; a rotation that only swaps one F4 for another is refused and the whole group is re-solved.
A coffee table is placed between the sofa and its TV as part of the seating group; a drawn table that is not on that axis is re-solved with the group rather than moved by hand.
A TV unit is placed with its back on a wall and its front facing the seating group; a rotation that trades its off-wall fault for a facing fault is refused and the group is re-solved.
A sofa is placed with its back on a wall; when no free wall span exists within the drawn-lock, the room's AI pieces are re-solved so the sofa lands on a wall span.
An armchair is placed within 2.50 m of and facing the coffee table of its group; a drawn armchair that is out of range is re-solved with the group rather than moved by hand.
The free zone in front of a sofa is kept clear of other group members; a blocking piece is re-solved with the group.
A nightstand is placed beside the bed head, clear of the window; when the drawn spot blocks the window and the swap/move options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.
A wardrobe is placed with ≥ 0.80 m clear in front; when the drawn spot leaves only 0.66 m and the swap/move options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.
A nightstand is placed beside the bed head, clear of the window; when the drawn spot blocks the window and the move/remove/swap options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.
A dining table is placed clear of the window (sill + 0.05 m); when the drawn spot blocks the window, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.
A dining chair is placed clear of the window (sill + 0.05 m); when the drawn spot blocks the window, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.
A room's type is set from its furniture set; when the set mixes living and dining pieces, the room is typed living and the dining group is placed as a sub-group, not by retyping the room.
A TV unit is placed with its back on a wall; when the drawn spot is 1.01 m off the wall and the relayout candidates keep the fault, the room's AI pieces are re-solved with a different candidate.

The inspector's render-quality finding must name the piece's actual type and module; a parametric kitchen cabinet (kitchen_run) is not a 'shoe cabinet' and its flat parametric look is expected, not a wrong_model defect.

The agent stage must not drop decor pieces (potted_plant, armchair, side_table) that the decor stage placed; every decor-stage piece must survive into the agent stage or be explicitly removed with a reason.

A planned kitchen piece (stove, sink_kitchen) that is part of a kitchen_run must be built as a distinct object in the scene; the build stage must not silently drop run members that have a planned model.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and the smaller is fully inside the larger, the reading stage must treat them as one piece (the larger) and mark the smaller as a duplicate, not as a separate piece to be built.

A drawn piece in a kitchen that no rule or model can type must be assigned a type from its size, room and neighbours (or explicitly marked not furniture) at the reading stage, so it is either built or explained; it must never be left as 'unknown' with no warning, review entry or symbol.
Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost stair or other element is visible to the auditor.
Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost element is visible to the auditor.

A toilet in a bathroom must be placed so its centre is at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; when the drawn position cannot meet this and no library model fits, the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture set rather than leaving the clearance unmet.

A bathtub or shower in a bathroom must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; when the drawn position cannot meet this and no library model fits, the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture set rather than leaving the clearance unmet.
A drawn bathtub longer than its bay is a misread size: resize it to the bay and the code re-centres it for its front clearance.
A drawn shower longer than its bay is a misread size: resize it to the bay and the code re-centres it for its front clearance.
A toilet whose side clearance fails is a misread size: resize it to a real product width and the code re-centres it for the 0.38 m side clearance.
An interior view of a wet room must show every fixture of the room's set, not just the anchor.
An interior view of a bedroom must show the bed and its nightstands, the room's anchor set.
An interior view of a balcony must show its furniture, not a bare slab.
An interior view of a balcony must show its seating area, not a bare slab.
A kitchen run is completed with its missing members (fridge, sink, stove) around its drawn anchor.
An interior render of a room must frame the room's anchor piece (the bed in a bedroom, the fixtures in a bathroom) so the main element is visible, not cut out of the frame.
A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures (basin, toilet, bath/shower); a view that omits them is not a valid view of the room.
A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures; a view that omits the toilet is not client-ready.
A bathroom view must show the basin; omitting it makes the room look unfinished.
A bathroom render must show its main fixtures; a view that omits the basin, bath and toilet reads as a room without its fixtures.
A bedroom must be furnished with its bed as the anchor, headboard against a wall; a room furnished as a home office instead of a bedroom is a misread of the room's program.
A bathroom render must show its main fixtures (toilet, shower); a view that omits them is not functional.
A balcony render must show its main furniture group; a view that shows only plants reads as an empty slab.
An opening in the documents must be cut through its wall; an opening that is not cut is a geometry error.

The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (mirror, art, shelf) over a wall fixture (washbasin, mirror) that occupies the same wall extent; it must raise the item over the fixture, move it along the wall, or leave it out.

The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item over a wall fixture (washbasin) that occupies the same wall extent; it must raise the item over the fixture, move it along the wall, or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (desk wall unit, art) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (wall art) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (desk wall unit) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.

A wall-hung item (art, shelf, mirror) must not be placed over an opening (window, door) on the same wall; the placement pass must check the opening's horizontal extent and the item's vertical extent and move the item to a free span or omit it.
A wall-mounted item must not overlap an existing wall fixture (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) on the same wall; the placement pass must check for overlaps and move the item to a free span or omit it.

A room with a large outer wall span (e.g., > 3 m) must have at least one window or door on that span to avoid a blank facade; the layout stage must check for blank facade spans and add a window or door if the room's program allows it.
The camera set must include a frontal view of the entrance facade (+y) to show the main entrance and facade design.
When the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (steeper than 1:3), a retaining edge must be built to support the slope; the site stage must check for steep slopes and add a retaining edge if needed.
A stair flight with a run of > 0.72 m must have a handrail over the entire run; the build stage must check for handrails on stair flights and add them if missing.

A bathroom set must include all functional elements (taps, towel rail, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.
A bathroom set must include all functional elements (mirror, taps, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.
An interior camera view must show all doors in the room to ensure the door is visible and accessible.
A retaining wall supporting a raised garden bed must have a material that matches the surrounding facade to avoid looking unfinished and out of place.
A bathroom's program set (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) is incomplete when the washbasin has no mirror above it; the set must be completed, not just re-camered.
A bathroom whose washbasin is not in frame and has no mirror over it is an incomplete set; complete the set rather than re-camering a bare wall.
A bathroom render that shows no mirror over the basin and bare flat tile is an incomplete set; the furniture agent must add the missing members (mirror, styled surfaces) before the camera is judged.
A terrace furnished with only two plants is bare; the terrace program's lounge group must be placed so the outdoor space reads as designed.
A kitchen counter's top must be built at its working height (0.90-0.95 m); a model whose top sits above 0.97 m is a wrong model and must be swapped for one at working height.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub with taps, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single isolated object in a bare corner.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single object in a bare corner.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub with taps, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single isolated object.
A drawn piece turned 90 deg from its drawn orientation is a reading error; rotate it back to its drawn front.
An interior/terrace camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.
A side table on a terrace/balcony must be an outdoor-rated model (weather-resistant, scaled for the space); an indoor glass-top table is a wrong model for the zone.
An interior camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.
A retaining or terrace wall that supports a raised bed or deck must be given a finished cladding (stone, render or timber) that matches the house's facade family, never left as bare concrete.

Every door must open into a finished, furnished room with a floor material consistent with the room it serves; a door that opens onto a bare void with a mismatched floor is a build error to be corrected before render.
Every site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as a modelled outline with its own material and content; a drawn pool with no built outline is a site-build failure.
Every labelled site area (sunning terrace, deck) must be built as a modelled outline with paving; a labelled terrace with no built outline is a site-build failure.
A drawn parking area must be built with its outline and at least one car model per bay; a parking area with no outline and no cars is a site-build failure.
A paved strip along a glazed facade must run the full length of the facade; a half-run that stops short and lets grass reach the glass is a site-build error.
In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat paved strip, not a raised walled box; a raised terrace wall where a flat paving is required is a site-build error.

A site plan must connect the house to the outside: the drive or path must run to the plot boundary or a street, and the plot must show its boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or road, so the house is not left standing on an open lawn with a drive that leads nowhere.
An entrance canopy must be a finished element: it needs a fascia, a soffit and visible support (tie rods or brackets); a bare slab projecting from the wall is not a canopy.

A site plan must show the plot boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or a road reaching the house; a house standing alone on an empty lawn with a drive that leads nowhere is not a finished site.

A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its members (e.g. a long run of cabinets or a dining set) and type each, instead of leaving it as one untyped cluster.
A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its members and type each, instead of leaving it as one untyped cluster.

A door under a sloped ceiling must have at least 1.60 m of headroom at its wall; where the roof slope leaves less, the build must add a dormer or raise the roof at that spot, not lower the door to the roof line.

A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint (a low 0.60 x 0.25 m piece) must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.
A balcony/terrace of 15 m2 or more must be furnished with a full terrace_lounge set (seating group, table, plant), not a single armchair and side_table.

A room whose label names a game/activity/relaxation function (Oyun Aktivite Ve Dinlenme Odasi) and whose furniture is a living set must be typed 'living', not 'other'; 'other' is reserved for rooms with no recognisable program.
A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.
A daybed/bed-like piece is only acceptable in a bedroom or a room explicitly typed for sleeping; in a living/activity room a bed-like footprint must be typed as a sofa or chaise, not a daybed.

A site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built with its outline and tracked in the site-area record even when its geometry is generated by the model; 'NOT built (no outline)' is only valid when the documents do not draw the area.

A bench (or any piece) whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces a wall, the piece is placed with its back to that wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.

A sofa whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces the most open floor, the piece is placed with its back to the opposite wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.
An interior camera of a wet room must frame the room's main fixtures (basin, toilet, shower/bath) from a free standing point with headroom, never a corner or a single fixture's edge.
A corridor camera must show the doors and the space as a whole from a free point, not a wall section and a single cabinet.
A kitchen's styled surfaces must include small worktop items and the upper cabinets/hood in frame; a bare worktop with only a fruit bowl is not a finished kitchen.
A kitchen run is not complete without its upper cabinets/hood and a styled worktop; the upper wall must not be left as an empty void.
A room's seating group (sofa, armchairs) must be one coordinated set in style and colour, not three mismatched lines.
A living seating group must be anchored by a large area rug under it; a bare floor under the sofa and coffee table is not a finished living room.
The view through a living room's glazing onto an outdoor terrace must show a furnished, designed terrace, not a flat empty lawn.
Coffee and side tables in a living room must carry styled objects (books, vases, small decor) so the surfaces read as lived-in, not bare.
A living/dining room needs a feature wall (slatted wood or paneling) to add depth; flat untextured concrete/paint is too raw for a stylish look.
A room's furniture must share a cohesive wood-tone palette; a dark walnut table clashing with light oak and mid-tone pieces is a mismatched set.
A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, basin) from a free point, not a door frame and vanity corner.
A bathroom camera must show the room's main group (basin, toilet, cabinet) from a free point, not a corner and the edge of the bathtub.
A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet, basin) from a free point, not a vanity corner.
An interior camera must not be positioned directly in front of a door leaf that fills the frame and obscures the room.
A bedroom window must have full-height two-layer curtains (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a bare window is not a finished bedroom.
A bedroom needs a feature wall (fluted or slatted wood panelling) behind the bed to anchor it; flat untextured paint is not a finished bedroom.
Every entrance hall and corridor must include a warm accent light (pendant or sconce) in its lighting set, not only the general ceiling light, so renders show layered warm light.

A wardrobe model whose mirrored door reflects a furnished room that does not exist in the scene must not be used; wardrobe models must have plain or non-reflective doors (or a reflection that matches the room).
Every exterior window in a living or bedroom space must carry a curtain or sheer on a track in the render set, so daylight and the view are framed and the wall does not read as flat paint.
Every living or dining group must sit on a rug sized to anchor the seating/dining cluster, so the floor does not read as bare and unfinished.

A drawn outdoor living area (sun terrace, pool deck) is built as a furnished outdoor room (seating, planters, paving) from its outline; a site render must show the outdoor space as designed, not a bare yard.
The main entrance door is rendered as a distinct, styled entrance (leaf, frame, canopy or accent) so the facade's entrance point is clearly readable in an exterior render.
A drawn pool and its deck are built as a cohesive outdoor room (seating, dining or fire pit, planters), not a pool with random loungers.
A bedroom floor specified as herringbone in the reference is rendered with a herringbone wood look, not a plain plank.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group (washbasin, toilet, cabinet) so the room reads as a designed space, not a tight crop of one corner.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet) so the layout and design are visible, not a close-up of the vanity and door.
A feature wall behind seating in a living room is rendered with a paneled or slatted finish, not a single flat paint colour.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group so the room reads as a whole, not a close-up of a corner.
An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a designed entry, not a close-up of a corner and door frame.

Seating pieces in a living room group must share a coherent style and colour family; a brown leather armchair is swapped for a minimal/modern armchair that matches the white sofa and black lounge chair.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group (bathtub, toilet, cabinet) so the room reads as a whole, not a close-up of a blank wall and toilet roll.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet) so the layout is visible, not a close-up that fails to show the room.
An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a styled entry, not a tight, low-angle shot of a corner and door.
An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a styled corridor, not a bare, unfinished corridor.
The site environment (lawn, planting, paving) is rendered as a designed landscape with texture and planting, not a bare, untextured surface.
A terrace floor is rendered with a designed outdoor floor material (paving stone, decking, or similar), not a bare, untextured grey slab.

The site stage must build the drawn landscape (pools, platforms, trees, parking and sunning areas) with textured ground, planting and hardscape, not a flat untextured plane, so exterior and terrace renders read as a finished environment.
A seating group (armchairs plus side table) must use models from the same design family so the set reads as designed, not as mismatched pieces.
A shoe cabinet in a hall must be a closed, finished cabinet (doors, styling) that matches a designed hall, not a bare open-cubby parametric placeholder.
A living room seating group must use models from the same design family (matching wood tones and style) so the room does not mix three different design languages.
A kitchen render must show a believable appliance (handles, panels) and styled surfaces; a featureless box or empty counter fails the client test.
A fridge model must have visible handles and panels to read as a real appliance, not a featureless box.
A kitchen render must not show broken or misplaced appliances; the fridge must be on the floor, not the counter.
A living room render must have a cohesive color palette; a single clashing accent (like a neon rug) fails the client test.
A dining set must mix bench and upholstered/wood chairs, not repeated identical plastic chairs.
A living room render must have a cohesive color palette; a single clashing accent (like a hot-pink rug) fails the client test.
A bedroom render must have layered styling (rug, curtains, art, lamps) and a neutral wall color; a loud green wall and bare surfaces fail the client test.
A shoe cabinet must be a believable piece of furniture, not a crude low-poly metal frame.
A window in a styled room must have layered curtains (sheer + drape), not a single flat drape.
A bedroom render must show the bed and nightstand as anchors; a room without them reads as an office.
A nightstand must be styled with lamps, books, or decorative objects to make the room feel lived-in.
An armchair in a neutral palette must not be a loud accent (like orange) that clashes with the rest of the set.
A window view must show a believable outdoor scene, not a flat grey void with lollipop trees.
Two armchairs in a seating group must be the same model and cushion color to read as a designed set.
A side table must be a believable piece of furniture, not a toy-like disc with random pegs.
A flush ceiling light must be at least 2.5 m from a pendant light to avoid reading as two lights together.
A fixture under a sloped ceiling is capped at the slope height at its footprint; the cap is independent of the drawn size check, so a size refusal must not block the height fix.

When one room outline carries the labels of two or more rooms, the reading must split it at the missing wall before room assignment; a label with no matching room outline is a lost-room signal, not a duplicate.
A balcony or terrace with drawn furniture must have that furniture built and visible; an empty outdoor room is a fit failure, not a camera failure.
A stair opening in a hall or landing that drops to a lower level must be built with a guardrail or barrier along its open edge; the guard is part of the stair's set, not an optional detail.
A fixture under a sloped ceiling must be a model whose height fits the headroom at its position; the shower's height is checked against the roof, not just its drawn footprint.
An interior camera must be posed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main group; a black frame means the pose is inside geometry and must be re-picked.
A soft seat's facing bodies must be joined so no part stands more than 1 cm apart; the build stage's join step is responsible for this.
A soft seat's back, back cushion and arms must rest against its seat with no gap over 5 mm; the build stage's rest plan is responsible for this.
Scene geometry checks (S1) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.
Scene geometry checks (S2) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.
Scene geometry checks (S4) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.
Scene geometry checks (S6) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.
A scene check that fails on a level must be re-run after the level's pieces are corrected; the build stage owns the scene assembly.
When an armchair's orientation is refused because rotating it breaks its group facing, the whole seating group must be re-solved so the armchair faces the group and the coffee table.
A tv_unit that stands behind the back of a seat and cannot be rotated without leaving the room outline must be re-placed by the room solver so its back is on a wall and it faces the seating.
A wardrobe that pokes through the room outline by a few centimetres should be swapped for a model whose depth fits the wall bay.
When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every single move is refused, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit so the table clears the chairs.
An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the room solver so the walkway is clear.
A sofa_corner whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the room solver so the walkway is clear.
When an armchair's orientation is refused because rotating it breaks its group facing or faces a wall, the whole seating group must be re-solved.
A tv_unit that stands behind the back of a seat and cannot be rotated (back off wall) or swapped (fit rules) must be re-placed by the room solver against a wall facing the seating.
When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every single move is refused, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit.
A stove whose back is a few centimetres off the wall is a misread centre; the code should snap it to the nearest valid wall spot.
A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in front of the counter must be re-solved by the room solver so the run is placed to give the required aisle.

A wardrobe (or any storage with a door or drawer front) placed against a wall must keep at least 0.80 m of clear floor in front of its opening face; the solver must reject any wall span shorter than the piece plus that clearance and, when no span fits, flag the room for a smaller or different storage piece rather than placing it with a blocked front.
A seating group's front clearance must be kept free of other pieces; the solver must not place a piece inside the front use zone of a sofa or armchair.
A nightstand must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs at the head of the bed on the free side.
A dining table must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs away from the glazing.
A chair must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs at the table, away from the glazing.
An armchair must face the seating group, not stand behind the back of another piece.
A tv_unit must have its back on a wall; it must not float in the middle of the room.
A sofa's long side is its front; it must not be turned 90° against its product size.
An armchair's front clearance must be kept free of other pieces.
A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; if the agent drops it, it must be re-added.
The agent stage must not drop a placed decor piece without recording it; a piece present after the decor stage and absent after the agent stage is a loss to be restored, not silently removed.

A stove that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

A sink_kitchen that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 15% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.
A small piece drawn 80% or more inside a larger seating piece (armchair, sofa) is its seat cushion or built-in element, not a separate piece; it is dropped as a detail of the larger piece.
none

A room whose program is a stair core (stair fills the room, no free floor point) is not given an interior camera; it is shown by the adjacent hall's view instead, and the camera stage must skip it rather than report it as a lost view.

A drawn block in a kitchen whose size matches a small appliance (roughly 0.2-0.6 m) that the furniture vocabulary does not type must be recorded with an explicit 'appliance, not modelled' note (or a dedicated appliance type) so it is neither silently dropped nor left unexplained.

A layer whose name is a stair section or elevation view (A-MERDIVEN, A-merdiven görünüş) is a detail view, not plan furniture: the reading classifies it as a detail view and feeds it to the stair reader, and the ledger does not flag it as lost when the stair it documents is built.

A layer whose name is a decorative or sanitary fixture detail view (Deko_Vitrifiye, Piu_Vitrifiye) is a detail view, not plan furniture: the reading classifies it as a detail view and the ledger does not flag it as lost.
A stove drawn with a small gap behind it (its back parallel to the wall) belongs on the wall: the reading snaps its back onto the wall instead of leaving a visible gap.
A shower drawn with a small gap behind it (its back parallel to the wall) belongs on the wall: the reading snaps its back onto the wall instead of leaving a visible gap.
A toilet whose centre is closer than 0.38 m to a side wall or fixture is misread: the reading moves it to the nearest valid spot that gives the required side clearance.
A shower with less than 0.53 m clear in front is misread: the reading moves it to the nearest valid spot that gives the required front clearance.

A toilet is placed so its centre is at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot rather than swapped for a model that still fails the clearance.
A bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot.
A shower must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot.
An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.
A bedroom must show its bed as the anchor; if the bed cannot be placed with the required clearances (0.60 m along the sides, headboard on a wall), the room is re-laid out so the bed fits.
An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, shower) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.
An interior camera of a balcony/terrace must show the room's main furniture (seating, side table) so the render reads as a designed outdoor living space.
An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, washbasin, shower) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.
An interior camera of a bedroom must show the bed as the anchor so the render reads as a bedroom.
An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, bathtub, washbasin) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.
An interior camera of a wet room must frame its fixtures (basin, toilet, shower/bath); a view that omits the basin makes the room read as unfinished.
A kitchen's run must be completed with its missing members (fridge, sink, stove, counter); a run without a fridge is not a kitchen.
A bedroom must be furnished as a bedroom (bed, nightstands, wardrobe); a desk-and-chair layout without a visible bed is a misread of the room's program.
An exterior render must show a real ground plane and site context (trees, hedge, court); a flat grey gradient reads as a placeholder.
Every opening must be cut through its wall; an opening whose ray hits the wall is not built.
A wall-mounted decor item must not overlap a wall fixture (basin, mirror, cabinet) on the same wall; the wall-item pass must raise it, move it along the wall, or drop it.
A wall-mounted decor item must not hang over a window opening; the wall-item pass must move it to a free wall span or drop it.

A hung decor item must never be placed on the wall span occupied by a washbasin or its mirror; the resolve pass must skip that span and use the next free wall, or omit the item if no free span exists.
Any outer wall span of a habitable room longer than 3 m must contain at least one window or door; the layout stage must add an opening if the drawing does not provide one.
Every project must include at least one frontal exterior camera view of the main entrance facade.
If the terrain slope is steeper than 1:3, the build stage must include a retaining edge or stepped foundation to support the structure.
Outdoor terrace furniture must use models rated for outdoor use (weather-resistant materials).
Indoor lighting fixtures (floor lamps) must not be placed on outdoor terraces; use outdoor-rated lighting instead.
Indoor storage furniture (bookshelves) must not be placed on outdoor terraces.
The inspector must read the room id of the target piece from the facts before judging its placement; a piece in an indoor living room is not on the terrace.

Every exterior door must be rendered with a modelled leaf and frame that match the window frames' material, and the space beyond an exterior door must be lit and textured (not a dark void) in the render.
Every door leaf and frame must be assigned a material that matches the project's window frame material (e.g. light wood) so that doors do not read as placeholder slabs.

A bathroom shower or bathtub model must include visible taps, a drain, and at least one accessory (towel rail or shelf) in its render; if the library model lacks these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures or choose a model that includes them.
Every washbasin in a bathroom must be rendered with a mirror above it; if the library model does not include a mirror, the building stage must place a mirror as a separate fixture above the basin.
Every interior camera view of a room must show at least one door or window of that room, so the viewer can orient themselves.

Every exterior camera view must be positioned outside the building envelope, at a distance of at least 1.5 m from the nearest facade, at eye height (1.6 m) or an aerial height, and must not be under the roof overhang.
Every exterior wall, including retaining walls, must be assigned a material that matches the building's facade material so that no bare concrete slabs are visible.
Every bathroom must have a complete bathroom_set including a mirror above the washbasin and a towel rail; if the set is incomplete, the building stage must add the missing members.
The inspector must verify that the bathroom_set members are actually missing before flagging a missing_member finding; if the set is complete, the finding is a false alarm.
Every interior camera view of a bathroom must show the main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) so the room reads as designed.

Every bathroom must have a mirror above the washbasin and at least one styled surface (accent wall, shelf, or accessory); if the library models do not include these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures.

Every outdoor scene must include textured ground (grass, paving, or gravel), at least 3 trees or shrubs with visible foliage, and a horizon that is not a hard line; the render stage must use high-quality ground and vegetation assets.

Every outdoor furniture piece must use a model that matches the project's style (e.g. scandinavian, modern) and has visible texture or design detail; plain generic models are not acceptable for outdoor scenes.
Every terrace or balcony must have a complete terrace_lounge group (at least 2 seating pieces, 1 table, and 2 plants) so it reads as a designed outdoor space.

A kitchen counter (kitchen_counter) is built at its standard working height (top at 0.90-0.95 m) regardless of the drawn footprint's height; a drawn counter taller than its working height is a misread of a tall unit or a wall cabinet, not a counter, and must be retyped or resized, never built as a counter at the drawn height.

A site area labelled as a pool (havuz) in the documents must be built as a pool outline in the model; if the site holds multiple pools, each documented pool area is built with its own outline and water surface, not left as an unbuilt label.
A site area labelled as a sunning terrace (guneslenme alani) in the documents must be built as a paved terrace outline in the model, not left as an unbuilt label.

A site area labelled as a parking area (otopark) in the documents must be built as a paved parking outline in the model, and at least one car model must be placed on it to show it is a parking area, not left as an unbuilt label with no cars.
Every interior door leaf is rendered open against its swing side by default; only entrance and terrace doors are closed.
A bathroom render must frame the vanity, mirror, shower and towel storage, not a bare wall above the tub.
A hall render must show the furnished room beyond, not be dominated by closed door slabs.
A living room must carry its full seating group (sculptural armchairs, round coffee table, lit TV console), not a plain sofa set.
A paved strip at the foot of a long glazed facade must run the full length of the facade, not stop short at one end.
The facade scheme is white render over a stone base, not stone from base to eaves.
In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat pale paved strip, not a raised walled terrace box.
A paved drive or stair path must lead on to the plot edge or a street, not end at the lawn.
An entrance canopy must carry a fascia, soffit and tie rods or brackets, not be a bare slab stuck out of the wall.
A house on a plot must show fenced neighbouring plots and a road coming to it; the drive must lead somewhere.
A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; it must be split into its members and typed individually, not left untyped.
A door under a sloped ceiling needs at least 1.60 m of headroom; where the roof slope leaves less, a dormer or raised roof must be added at that spot.

A door under a sloped ceiling whose headroom is under 1.60 m at its wall and within 0.5 m along it must be flagged for a dormer or raised roof; the building stage must not lower the door to the roof line and leave it unusable.

When a bedroom's drawn bed leaves less than the nightstand depth (0.60 m) on one side, the sleeping set is complete with a single nightstand on the free side; do not flag the missing second nightstand as a defect.
A large living room (>= 40 m2) may carry a wardrobe as living_storage; do not flag a wardrobe in a living room of that size as a wrong-type placement.

A wet fixture is typed from the drawn fixture in its own room, not from the size table of a piece in another room; when the plan shows a shower, the wet fixture is a shower even if a size match elsewhere suggests a tub.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's full fixture set (WC, basin, storage, bath/shower) from a corner with headroom, never a single fixture in isolation.
A bathroom whose documents draw a tub block (parent-bath set) must be built with a bathtub, not a shower, even when the room is small.
A shoe_cabinet belongs at an entrance hall, not at a top-floor landing; a landing hall takes a console or storage instead.
A balcony/terrace larger than about 12 m2 must be furnished as a seating set (at least two seats plus a table), never a single chair.
A WC flush plate must render as a slim rounded dual-flush plate with a small and a large button, never as a frame holding two flat panes.
An accent wall finish (e.g. vertical slats) is applied to at most one wall of a room, never to all walls of a room or to every room.
An interior camera must frame at least one fixture or piece of value, never a bare wall, corner or switch.
A facade scheme with a stone base and a render body must keep the stone to the base/plinth and apply the render (e.g. white) to the upper walls, never stone from base to eaves.
An interior camera must frame the room's built fixtures; a black/empty view is a camera failure, not a missing room.
A site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built with an outline and tracked as a site area, even when its geometry is already present in the model.
The sheets stage must resolve every sheet question before ending; a run that ends 'pending' with open questions has not finished its reading.
A sofa's front is its long side facing the most open room; a front read on its short side (an AI front) is a reading error and must be corrected to the long side.
A drawn piece whose size and wall position match a console table (long, narrow, back on a wall) must be typed console_table, not bench, so its front faces the room and its back rests on the wall.
The big loop must run additional cycles when the first cycle yields no gain, to allow the agent to resolve remaining orientation and placement conflicts.
A sofa drawn with its long side against a wall must have its front facing into the room (away from the wall), not along the long side.
A sofa without a front must have its front set to face the most open floor, towards its partner.
An armchair without a front must have its front set to face away from its wall or towards its partner.
An interior camera must be placed at a free point clear of walls and tall proxies, showing the required elements.
A table_coffee built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.
A tv_unit built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.
A tall_cabinet built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.

When no library model passes the fit rules for a piece, the fitter must not silently keep the parametric mesh as if it were a library pick; it must either relax the height/cap tolerance to accept the nearest library model or flag the piece as unbuildable, never report a library-level build from a parametric fallback.

When a tall piece is placed under a sloped ceiling and its height exceeds the local ceiling clearance, the fitter must either lower the piece to a location with sufficient headroom, swap to a model within the clearance, or flag the placement as infeasible; it must not keep a parametric mesh that violates the ceiling.
A camera of a stair room must be posed from the landing or the hall side so the flight is visible, never from a point inside the stair core.
Views flagged for review are a queue, not a defect; each is resolved by the specific camera or door finding that names it.
Every inside door is built open by default (leaf out of the wall) unless a camera or privacy rule closes it; the build records a leaf state for each door it places.
When a camera looks through an inside door into a room worth showing, the build opens that door (leaf out of the view) and records the state.

A nightstand is placed on the free side of the bed head, not in front of a window; when the bed head is against a window wall the nightstand goes on the opposite side or the window is treated as the head wall.
A toilet is built with its base at floor level (lowest point within -0.005..+0.01 m of the room floor); a model whose base sits above the floor is rejected at fit, not swapped in.
A bathroom washbasin is always built with a mirror above it as part of the vanity set; the bathroom set is incomplete without the mirror.
A tv_unit is placed with its back on a wall; when the only free wall span is blocked by doors or windows, the unit is placed on the next free span or the room is flagged, never left floating.
A coffee table is placed in the seating group with a clear gap to every armchair; when the group is too tight, the armchair is re-posed, not the table pushed into it.
A wardrobe is placed with at least 0.80 m clear in front; when the room cannot give that, the wardrobe is moved to a wall with more clearance or the room is flagged, never left short.
A drawn armchair in a seating group is re-posed (rotated) to face the group and clear its front zone before it is moved; a move beyond the drawn lock is refused, so rotation is the first fix.

rules_proposed.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g. SALON + AÇIK MUTFAK), the reading must split the outline into the separate rooms each label names, instead of keeping one merged room and dropping the other labels.
Every room label the documents name on a level must map to a distinct room in the model; a label whose area and anchor do not match any built room is a lost room, not a duplicate.

The agent stage must not drop decor pieces (potted_plant, armchair, side_table) that the decor stage placed; every decor-stage piece must survive into the agent stage or be explicitly removed with a reason.

A planned kitchen piece (stove, sink_kitchen) that is part of a kitchen_run must be built as a distinct object in the scene; the build stage must not silently drop run members that have a planned model.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and the smaller is fully inside the larger, the reading stage must treat them as one piece (the larger) and mark the smaller as a duplicate, not as a separate piece to be built.

A drawn piece in a kitchen that no rule or model can type must be assigned a type from its size, room and neighbours (or explicitly marked not furniture) at the reading stage, so it is either built or explained; it must never be left as 'unknown' with no warning, review entry or symbol.
Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost stair or other element is visible to the auditor.
Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost element is visible to the auditor.

When one room outline carries the labels of two or more rooms, the reading must split it at the missing wall before room assignment; a label with no matching room outline is a lost-room signal, not a duplicate.
A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; if the agent drops it, it must be re-added.
The agent stage must not drop a placed decor piece without recording it; a piece present after the decor stage and absent after the agent stage is a loss to be restored, not silently removed.

A stove that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

A sink_kitchen that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 15% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.
A small piece drawn 80% or more inside a larger seating piece (armchair, sofa) is its seat cushion or built-in element, not a separate piece; it is dropped as a detail of the larger piece.

rules_proposed.rule: An opening in the documents must be cut through its wall; an opening that is not cut is a geometry error.

A wall-mounted item must not overlap an existing wall fixture (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) on the same wall; the placement pass must check for overlaps and move the item to a free span or omit it.

A room with a large outer wall span (e.g., > 3 m) must have at least one window or door on that span to avoid a blank facade; the layout stage must check for blank facade spans and add a window or door if the room's program allows it.
The camera set must include a frontal view of the entrance facade (+y) to show the main entrance and facade design.
When the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (steeper than 1:3), a retaining edge must be built to support the slope; the site stage must check for steep slopes and add a retaining edge if needed.
A stair flight with a run of > 0.72 m must have a handrail over the entire run; the build stage must check for handrails on stair flights and add them if missing.

A bathroom set must include all functional elements (taps, towel rail, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.
A bathroom set must include all functional elements (mirror, taps, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.
An interior camera view must show all doors in the room to ensure the door is visible and accessible.
A retaining wall supporting a raised garden bed must have a material that matches the surrounding facade to avoid looking unfinished and out of place.
A bathroom's program set (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) is incomplete when the washbasin has no mirror above it; the set must be completed, not just re-camered.
A bathroom whose washbasin is not in frame and has no mirror over it is an incomplete set; complete the set rather than re-camering a bare wall.
A bathroom render that shows no mirror over the basin and bare flat tile is an incomplete set; the furniture agent must add the missing members (mirror, styled surfaces) before the camera is judged.
A terrace furnished with only two plants is bare; the terrace program's lounge group must be placed so the outdoor space reads as designed.
A kitchen counter's top must be built at its working height (0.90-0.95 m); a model whose top sits above 0.97 m is a wrong model and must be swapped for one at working height.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub with taps, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single isolated object in a bare corner.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single object in a bare corner.

An interior/terrace camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.
A side table on a terrace/balcony must be an outdoor-rated model (weather-resistant, scaled for the space); an indoor glass-top table is a wrong model for the zone.
An interior camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.
A retaining or terrace wall that supports a raised bed or deck must be given a finished cladding (stone, render or timber) that matches the house's facade family, never left as bare concrete.

Every door must open into a finished, furnished room with a floor material consistent with the room it serves; a door that opens onto a bare void with a mismatched floor is a build error to be corrected before render.
Every site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as a modelled outline with its own material and content; a drawn pool with no built outline is a site-build failure.
Every labelled site area (sunning terrace, deck) must be built as a modelled outline with paving; a labelled terrace with no built outline is a site-build failure.
A drawn parking area must be built with its outline and at least one car model per bay; a parking area with no outline and no cars is a site-build failure.
A paved strip along a glazed facade must run the full length of the facade; a half-run that stops short and lets grass reach the glass is a site-build error.
In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat paved strip, not a raised walled box; a raised terrace wall where a flat paving is required is a site-build error.

A site plan must connect the house to the outside: the drive or path must run to the plot boundary or a street, and the plot must show its boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or road, so the house is not left standing on an open lawn with a drive that leads nowhere.
An entrance canopy must be a finished element: it needs a fascia, a soffit and visible support (tie rods or brackets); a bare slab projecting from the wall is not a canopy.

A site plan must show the plot boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or a road reaching the house; a house standing alone on an empty lawn with a drive that leads nowhere is not a finished site.
A stair opening in a hall or landing that drops to a lower level must be built with a guardrail or barrier along its open edge; the guard is part of the stair's set, not an optional detail.
An exterior render must show a real ground plane and site context (trees, hedge, court); a flat grey gradient reads as a placeholder.
Every opening must be cut through its wall; an opening whose ray hits the wall is not built.
A wall-mounted decor item must not overlap a wall fixture (basin, mirror, cabinet) on the same wall; the wall-item pass must raise it, move it along the wall, or drop it.
A wall-mounted decor item must not hang over a window opening; the wall-item pass must move it to a free wall span or drop it.

A hung decor item must never be placed on the wall span occupied by a washbasin or its mirror; the resolve pass must skip that span and use the next free wall, or omit the item if no free span exists.
Any outer wall span of a habitable room longer than 3 m must contain at least one window or door; the layout stage must add an opening if the drawing does not provide one.
Every project must include at least one frontal exterior camera view of the main entrance facade.
If the terrain slope is steeper than 1:3, the build stage must include a retaining edge or stepped foundation to support the structure.
Outdoor terrace furniture must use models rated for outdoor use (weather-resistant materials).
Indoor lighting fixtures (floor lamps) must not be placed on outdoor terraces; use outdoor-rated lighting instead.
Indoor storage furniture (bookshelves) must not be placed on outdoor terraces.
The inspector must read the room id of the target piece from the facts before judging its placement; a piece in an indoor living room is not on the terrace.

Every exterior door must be rendered with a modelled leaf and frame that match the window frames' material, and the space beyond an exterior door must be lit and textured (not a dark void) in the render.
Every door leaf and frame must be assigned a material that matches the project's window frame material (e.g. light wood) so that doors do not read as placeholder slabs.

A bathroom shower or bathtub model must include visible taps, a drain, and at least one accessory (towel rail or shelf) in its render; if the library model lacks these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures or choose a model that includes them.
Every washbasin in a bathroom must be rendered with a mirror above it; if the library model does not include a mirror, the building stage must place a mirror as a separate fixture above the basin.
Every interior camera view of a room must show at least one door or window of that room, so the viewer can orient themselves.

Every exterior camera view must be positioned outside the building envelope, at a distance of at least 1.5 m from the nearest facade, at eye height (1.6 m) or an aerial height, and must not be under the roof overhang.
Every exterior wall, including retaining walls, must be assigned a material that matches the building's facade material so that no bare concrete slabs are visible.
Every bathroom must have a complete bathroom_set including a mirror above the washbasin and a towel rail; if the set is incomplete, the building stage must add the missing members.
The inspector must verify that the bathroom_set members are actually missing before flagging a missing_member finding; if the set is complete, the finding is a false alarm.
Every interior camera view of a bathroom must show the main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) so the room reads as designed.

Every bathroom must have a mirror above the washbasin and at least one styled surface (accent wall, shelf, or accessory); if the library models do not include these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures.

Every outdoor scene must include textured ground (grass, paving, or gravel), at least 3 trees or shrubs with visible foliage, and a horizon that is not a hard line; the render stage must use high-quality ground and vegetation assets.

Every outdoor furniture piece must use a model that matches the project's style (e.g. scandinavian, modern) and has visible texture or design detail; plain generic models are not acceptable for outdoor scenes.
Every terrace or balcony must have a complete terrace_lounge group (at least 2 seating pieces, 1 table, and 2 plants) so it reads as a designed outdoor space.

A kitchen counter (kitchen_counter) is built at its standard working height (top at 0.90-0.95 m) regardless of the drawn footprint's height; a drawn counter taller than its working height is a misread of a tall unit or a wall cabinet, not a counter, and must be retyped or resized, never built as a counter at the drawn height.

A site area labelled as a pool (havuz) in the documents must be built as a pool outline in the model; if the site holds multiple pools, each documented pool area is built with its own outline and water surface, not left as an unbuilt label.
A site area labelled as a sunning terrace (guneslenme alani) in the documents must be built as a paved terrace outline in the model, not left as an unbuilt label.

A site area labelled as a parking area (otopark) in the documents must be built as a paved parking outline in the model, and at least one car model must be placed on it to show it is a parking area, not left as an unbuilt label with no cars.
Every interior door leaf is rendered open against its swing side by default; only entrance and terrace doors are closed.
A bathroom render must frame the vanity, mirror, shower and towel storage, not a bare wall above the tub.
A hall render must show the furnished room beyond, not be dominated by closed door slabs.
A living room must carry its full seating group (sculptural armchairs, round coffee table, lit TV console), not a plain sofa set.
A paved strip at the foot of a long glazed facade must run the full length of the facade, not stop short at one end.
The facade scheme is white render over a stone base, not stone from base to eaves.
In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat pale paved strip, not a raised walled terrace box.
A paved drive or stair path must lead on to the plot edge or a street, not end at the lawn.
An entrance canopy must carry a fascia, soffit and tie rods or brackets, not be a bare slab stuck out of the wall.
A house on a plot must show fenced neighbouring plots and a road coming to it; the drive must lead somewhere.

rules_proposed.rule: A tall wet-room fixture (shower, tub) under a sloped ceiling must be capped or swapped to a model whose height fits the slope at its position; nothing inside may cross the roof (UL128).
A sectional sofa's parts must be joined (within 1 cm); parts standing apart are a build defect, fixed by re-joining, not by swapping the model.
An armchair's back and arms must rest against its seat (within 5 mm); a gap is a build defect, fixed by re-planning the rests, not by swapping the model.
Scene geometry checks (S1) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S2) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S4) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.
Scene geometry checks (S6) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

When an armchair is placed behind the back of a sofa and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that lowers plausibility is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.

When a tv_unit is placed behind the back of a piece and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that pushes it through the room outline is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.
A wardrobe that reaches through the room outline, even by a small depth, must be re-placed or resized so it stays within the room; the fit stage must keep all pieces inside the room outline.

When a table_coffee overlaps an armchair, the fit stage must re-place one of them so they do not overlap; if move_piece is refused because the overlap persists or max_tries is reached, the agent must try a different position or swap a model.
An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; the fit stage must ensure every piece's front use zone is reachable.

A sofa_corner whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; if swap_model is refused because the asset is unusable, the agent must try a different model or re-place the piece.

A seating group whose members cannot all face each other and keep a 0.60 m walkway from the door is re-solved as one unit (relayout) rather than rotated piece by piece, which only trades one orientation error for another.
A piece that crosses a room outline by 0.02 m or less is within tolerance and is not a finding.
When a coffee table overlaps a chair and every single-piece move is refused (max_tries), the seating group is re-solved as a unit so the table and chairs are placed together with clearances.

A piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the room's seating group, not by moving the single piece, which would break the group it belongs to.
A corner sofa whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the seating group; swapping to a smaller model is refused when the asset is unusable.
A stove whose back is not on a wall is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run as a unit so the counter, stove and sink are placed together against the wall with the required aisle.
A kitchen counter whose front aisle is under 0.90 m is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run so the counter is placed against the wall with a full aisle.
A sofa whose drawn footprint is 0.90 m wide by 2.13 m deep is a misread orientation: the piece is re-typed or re-placed so its long side is the seat depth, not the width.
A sofa whose back is 0.59 m off a wall and cannot be moved to a free wall span within the drawn-lock limit is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the sofa is placed against a wall.
An armchair that does not face its group is fixed by re-solving the seating group so all members face each other.
An armchair whose front zone is blocked by another armchair is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the two armchairs are placed with clear front zones.
A dining chair with under 0.81 m behind it is fixed by re-solving the dining group so the chairs have the required clearance to the wall or piece behind.
A seating group whose members are drawn overlapping or with blocked front zones must be re-solved as a unit, not rotated piece by piece.
A dining chair with less than 0.81 m behind it must be re-solved with its table, not nudged alone.

A coffee table not in front of the sofa must be re-solved with the seating group.

rules_proposed.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its members (e.g. a long run of cabinets or a dining set) and type each, instead of leaving it as one untyped cluster.

A door under a sloped ceiling must have at least 1.60 m of headroom at its wall; where the roof slope leaves less, the build must add a dormer or raise the roof at that spot, not lower the door to the roof line.

A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint (a low 0.60 x 0.25 m piece) must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.

A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.

rules_proposed.rule: A bench (or any piece) whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces a wall, the piece is placed with its back to that wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.

A sofa whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces the most open floor, the piece is placed with its back to the opposite wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.
The sheets stage must resolve every sheet question before ending; a run that ends 'pending' with open questions has not finished its reading.
A sofa's front is its long side facing the most open room; a front read on its short side (an AI front) is a reading error and must be corrected to the long side.
A drawn piece whose size and wall position match a console table (long, narrow, back on a wall) must be typed console_table, not bench, so its front faces the room and its back rests on the wall.
The big loop must run additional cycles when the first cycle yields no gain, to allow the agent to resolve remaining orientation and placement conflicts.
A sofa drawn with its long side against a wall must have its front facing into the room (away from the wall), not along the long side.
A sofa without a front must have its front set to face the most open floor, towards its partner.
An armchair without a front must have its front set to face away from its wall or towards its partner.
An interior camera must be placed at a free point clear of walls and tall proxies, showing the required elements.
A table_coffee built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.
A tv_unit built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.
A tall_cabinet built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.

When no library model passes the fit rules for a piece, the fitter must not silently keep the parametric mesh as if it were a library pick; it must either relax the height/cap tolerance to accept the nearest library model or flag the piece as unbuildable, never report a library-level build from a parametric fallback.

When a tall piece is placed under a sloped ceiling and its height exceeds the local ceiling clearance, the fitter must either lower the piece to a location with sufficient headroom, swap to a model within the clearance, or flag the placement as infeasible; it must not keep a parametric mesh that violates the ceiling.
A camera of a stair room must be posed from the landing or the hall side so the flight is visible, never from a point inside the stair core.
Views flagged for review are a queue, not a defect; each is resolved by the specific camera or door finding that names it.

rules_proposed.rule: A nightstand is placed on the free side of the bed head, not in front of a window; when the bed head is against a window wall the nightstand goes on the opposite side or the window is treated as the head wall.
A toilet is built with its base at floor level (lowest point within -0.005..+0.01 m of the room floor); a model whose base sits above the floor is rejected at fit, not swapped in.
A bathroom washbasin is always built with a mirror above it as part of the vanity set; the bathroom set is incomplete without the mirror.
A tv_unit is placed with its back on a wall; when the only free wall span is blocked by doors or windows, the unit is placed on the next free span or the room is flagged, never left floating.
A coffee table is placed in the seating group with a clear gap to every armchair; when the group is too tight, the armchair is re-posed, not the table pushed into it.
A wardrobe is placed with at least 0.80 m clear in front; when the room cannot give that, the wardrobe is moved to a wall with more clearance or the room is flagged, never left short.
A drawn armchair in a seating group is re-posed (rotated) to face the group and clear its front zone before it is moved; a move beyond the drawn lock is refused, so rotation is the first fix.
